title: Case study: video streaming
summary: Upload and transcoding pipeline, adaptive bitrate, CDN economics: requirements and estimation, API and data model, a segment-parallel transcoding DAG that survives failure, packaging and the bitrate ladder, CDN hit ratio and storage tiers for the long tail, view counts at scale, live as stretch.

units.title: Guided design: requirements, estimation, API, data model, high-level design
Deep dives: the transcoding DAG and its failures, packaging and adaptive bitrate, CDN economics and storage tiers, view counts; live as stretch

labs.title: Transcoding pipeline as a DAG: segment × rendition transcodes, per-segment packaging, manifest; bounded worker pool, retries with backoff, per-attempt timeouts, panic containment, idempotent resume, leak-free cancellation
Adaptive bitrate selection: safety factor, immediate down-switch, buffer-gated up-switch, panic to the lowest rendition

outcomes.text: Scope a video platform in six minutes: the clarifying questions whose answers change the design (VOD or live, user-generated or curated, upload-to-watch ratio, devices, time to playable, protection, viewer geography) and non-functional requirements with numbers.

Estimate concurrent viewers, peak egress in Tbps, egress bytes and cost per month, segment request rate, ingest, storage per minute across a bitrate ladder and per year, and transcode compute, and tie each number to a decision.

Design the API (idempotent resumable upload, playback returning a signed manifest URL, watch progress, batched playback events) and a data model that separates metadata from blobs, with deterministic, versioned, immutable object keys and an artifacts record as the processing truth.
Draw the high-level design with the upload, processing and playback paths traced, and justify every box by a requirement or a number.
Design the transcoding pipeline as a dependency graph: segment-level parallelism, dependency-driven scheduling with one owner, bounded workers, fairness across jobs and a fast path to playable.

Make the pipeline survive failure: classify failures, bounded retries with backoff and jitter, per-attempt timeouts, poison inputs to dead letters, idempotent resume from finished artifacts, and cancellation that leaks nothing.

Implement the pipeline (labs/c11/transcode): the DAG, a bounded worker pool, retries with backoff, per-attempt timeouts, panic containment, resume from a store of artifacts, progress and leak-free cancellation, passing under -race.

Explain packaging (HLS, DASH, CMAF, segment duration, aligned keyframes), bitrate-ladder design, and how a player adapts quality per segment (safety factor, immediate down-switch, buffer-gated up-switch, panic rule).

Reason about CDN economics and storage: egress dominates, byte hit ratio, cache keys and TTLs, shield tiers and request collapsing, head versus long tail, multi-CDN and ISP-embedded caches, storage tiers by last access and lazy rungs for the tail.

Design view counts and watch progress at scale: an event log with windowed aggregation, hot-key handling, a fast approximate display versus an exact batch recount, and last-writer-wins progress partitioned by user.
Implement an adaptive bitrate policy (labs/c11/abr) and explain per-title encoding and when it pays back.
Adapt the design for live streaming: a latency budget, real-time transcoding, low-latency HLS/DASH, playlist caching and collapsing, and redundant ingest.
